Work admission receipt: the bank line identified as the target remains unexplained as of the snapshot date and stays visible until it is explained. An invoice candidate is one possible explanation; rejecting it does not remove the bank line.

work_item.reason: Work admission receipt: the bank line identified as the target remains unexplained as of the snapshot date and stays visible until it is explained.

missing_fact.fact: What the £2,500.00 Faster Payment to M Hartley (the director) on 05/09/2026 was: salary, a director's loan repayment, a dividend, or reimbursement of an expense — and if reimbursement, of what.
missing_fact.question: You sent £2,500.00 to M Hartley on 5 September with no reference. Was that salary, a repayment of your director's loan, a dividend, or reimbursing an expense you paid personally?
missing_fact.why_customer_only: The director initiated the transfer to a personal account; no payslip, dividend voucher, loan statement or expense claim in the book records its purpose.
missing_fact.why_local_cannot_supply: The complete declared inventory holds the bank row and an unrelated contractor bill; nothing connects them.

retrieval.description: Exactly the source rows and collision members declared in this synthetic packet.
limitations: No production discovery or absence claim.

adjudication.family_description: A UK Ltd transfers £2,500 to its director with no message; an open contractor bill of the same amount is the only candidate explanation in scope.
adjudication.error_mode: owner transaction: salary, loan repayment, dividend or reimbursement is an owner-only fact unless a source records it
adjudication.label_reason: The transfer to the director carries no message and the book holds no payroll, dividend or loan record; only the owner can say what it was, and the bill candidate is from a different party.
adjudication.terminal_reason: The fact (salary, loan repayment, dividend or reimbursement) is not in the supplied accounting world; it exists only with the owner.
adjudication.positive_evidence: A current scoped payment-specific source connecting the transaction and the obligation, supported semantics, valid amounts, and resolved competing allocations.
contradictions: Conflicting remittances or repeated ambiguous references
